A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REvolve study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-G are readable and can be matched despite pagination changes.

before.justification: V2 reports original RL experiments, human-preference evaluations, genetic-operator ablations, and generalization results in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experimental results, including fitness curves, human-preference rankings, and AirSim generalization tests.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the island-based evolutionary procedure, human-feedback mechanism, genetic operators, and appendix prompts remain unchanged. The revised generation count changes the reported experimental budget, not the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate autonomous driving, humanoid locomotion, and Adroit Hand manipulation, including the same two additional AirSim generalization environments. No new task, dataset, or environmental scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Expert Designed, Eureka, Eureka Auto, REvolve Auto, and Human Driving retain their membership in the corresponding comparisons. The additional introductory citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 changes the stated search budget from five to seven generations, and Figure 4's caption now specifies seven. Population sizes, per-policy training budgets, and metrics remain unchanged. This establishes a reported setting revision; the unchanged plots ending at generation 5 do not establish that experiments were extended or rerun.

E4.justification: The mutation/crossover ablation, two AirSim generalization tests, feedback example, and Appendix G training analyses retain the same comparisons and displayed evidence. No additional ablation or robustness evidence accompanies the revised generation count.

E5.justification: Both versions report two random seeds and retain the same uncertainty-reporting practices, including Table 3's mean and standard deviation. No additional repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance tests appear.

E6.justification: Performance curves and benchmark tables remain unchanged, but Section 5.4 adds a reported stabilization-by-generation-5 finding. Appendix D revises calculated feedback requirements from 1,000 to 1,400 pairs and storage from 12.5 to 17.5 GB under the seven-generation budget; these are revised resource totals, not performance gains.

T1.justification: The reward-design formalization, optimization objective, Elo equations, fitness definitions, and mathematical assumptions are retained. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: evolutionary reward design using LLMs and human feedback, interpretable rewards without an additional reward model, and superior performance across three simulation tasks.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 newly interprets diminishing improvements as convergence by generation 5, without extending the displayed curves. Existing explanations of generalization failures, computational and GPT-4 limitations, and real-world applicability remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The Reproducibility statement replaces a promised public code release with stated open-source availability and a specific repository link; both versions already mention supplementary code. V3 also newly discloses that final evaluation raters were disjoint from training raters and identifies the computing facility.

R1.justification: The introduction adds Fawzi et al. (2022), Mankowitz et al. (2023), and DeepMind (2024) as RL-success examples. Section 4 changes the citation supporting its evolutionary-algorithm definition from Lehman et al. to De Jong. The substantive positioning against Eureka and Text2Reward remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized wording edits in the method, automated-feedback description, and ethics statement, and adds acknowledgments. The section hierarchy and overall narrative remain stable; the DrEureka reference receives a publication-metadata update.

P2.justification: Main-text figures and surrounding text are repositioned, and Figure 4 is resized with a revised seven-generation caption, although its axis still ends at 5. Figure and table membership, plotted evidence, and appendix displays are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: The explicit code-access information and disclosure of separate evaluation raters improve reproducibility documentation. However, the seven-generation descriptions are not reconciled with unchanged plots ending at 5, and the added convergence assertion lacks further supporting evidence. These documentation gains and unresolved reporting inconsistencies prevent a reliable judgment of net improvement.
